title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 48 (Variation of Shareholders’ Rights)

content.overview: Section 48 provides that where the share capital is divided into different classes, the rights attached to any class may be varied with the written consent of holders of not less than three-fourths of the issued shares of that class, or by a special resolution passed at a separate meeting of holders of that class, subject to the articles and the Act. Dissenting shareholders holding not less than ten per cent of the issued shares of that class may apply to the Tribunal to have the variation cancelled.
content.glance: Class rights may be varied by 3/4 consent or special resolution of the class; 10% dissenters may apply to the Tribunal to cancel the variation.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 48 (Variation of shareholders' rights). Where share capital is divided into classes, rights attached to a class may be varied by written consent of holders of at least three-fourths of the issued shares of that class or by special resolution at a separate class meeting, subject to the memorandum/articles and terms of issue. If the variation affects another class, that other class must also give three-fourths consent. Holders of at least 10% of the issued shares of the affected class who did not consent or vote in favour may apply to the Tribunal within 21 days after the consent or resolution; the variation has no effect unless and until confirmed by the Tribunal. The Tribunal's decision binds shareholders. The company must file a copy of the Tribunal order with the Registrar within 30 days. Subsection (5) provides the penalty for default: company fine ₹25,000–₹5,00,000; an officer in default may face imprisonment up to six months or a fine ₹25,000–₹5,00,000, or both. This is a class-rights procedure, not an ordinary alteration of share capital.

sections.heading: Variation mechanism and class terms
sections.body: Rights attached to a class may be varied by written consent of holders of at least three-fourths of the issued shares of that class or by special resolution at a separate class meeting, where the memorandum/articles provide for variation or, absent such provision, where the terms of issue do not prohibit it.

sections.heading: Rights of another class
sections.body: If a variation by one class affects the rights of another class, three-fourths consent of that other class must also be obtained and section 48 applies to that variation.

sections.heading: Dissenting holders and 21-day application
sections.body: Holders of at least 10% of the issued shares of a class who did not consent or vote in favour may apply to the Tribunal within 21 days after the consent or resolution. If an application is made, the variation has no effect unless and until the Tribunal confirms it.

sections.heading: Tribunal decision and filing
sections.body: The Tribunal's decision binds shareholders. The company must file a copy of the Tribunal order with the Registrar within 30 days of the order.

sections.heading: Penalty for default
sections.body: Subsection (5) provides a fine of ₹25,000 to ₹5,00,000 for the company. An officer in default may be imprisoned for up to six months or fined ₹25,000 to ₹5,00,000, or both.

examples.title: Class special resolution
examples.body: Preference shareholders pass a special resolution at a separate meeting to alter preferential dividend rights. Section 48 is engaged; dissenters with ≥10% may apply to the Tribunal.

examples.title: Dissenters’ challenge
examples.body: Shareholders holding 12% of a class did not consent to a rights variation and apply to the Tribunal under s. 48 to cancel it.

hypotheticals.question: A variation affects both preference shares and another class of shares. Is consent from only the first class enough?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The proviso requires three-fourths consent of the other affected class as well.

hypotheticals.question: A qualifying dissenting shareholder wants to challenge a class-rights variation. What deadline applies?
hypotheticals.analysis: The application to the Tribunal must be made within 21 days after the consent was given or the resolution was passed.

distinctions.title: Variation of rights (s. 48) vs voting rights (s. 47)
distinctions.left: How class rights may be changed and challenged
distinctions.right: Who votes on resolutions in the ordinary course

misconceptions.trap: Assuming a simple majority or Board resolution can vary class rights.
misconceptions.correction: Section 48 requires three-fourths written consent or a special resolution at a separate class meeting, subject to the statutory terms.

misconceptions.trap: Ignoring another class whose rights are affected.
misconceptions.correction: Three-fourths consent of the other affected class is also required.

misconceptions.trap: Omitting the 21-day dissenters' application period and 30-day Registrar filing.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the dissenters' application period?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Within 21 days after the consent was given or the resolution was passed.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When must the Tribunal order be filed with the Registrar?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Within 30 days of the date of the Tribunal's order.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the subsection (5) penalty?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Company: fine ₹25,000–₹5,00,000. Officer in default: imprisonment up to six months or fine ₹25,000–₹5,00,000, or both.
